label_policy: Command-side state expectations are independent of production replay. These scripted cases evaluate integrity, not model semantic decisions. Development/held-out designations identify scenario families, not a hidden quality test.

defaults.database: unique disposable local SQLite database per case

invariants: expected memberships, active threads, user pins and archive state match command-side model
memory titles and source filenames match commands
prior event IDs, sequence, timestamp, kind, origin, memory ID and payload remain unchanged
event IDs are unique; source, correction and citation references point backward to existing events
visible database memories and replayed archive state agree
reopening does not duplicate history or lose state

scenarios.expected: No duplicate memory or capture event.
Each revision cites its previous source; prior payloads remain immutable.
Source revision links skip metadata and preserve capture.
Archive is idempotent and restoration preserves memberships.

steps: assign first memory to two threads
scenarios.expected: Shared memory and other memberships remain visible.
Thread restoration does not alter memories or pins.
Invalid corrections are rejected without appending history.
Unrelated correction is preserved.
Stale undo rejected and latest title retained.

steps: assign first memory to second thread
scenarios.expected: Prior membership restored and explicit correction remains pinned.
Stale undo cannot overwrite newer placement.
Parents and memberships restored; pair blocked; repeated undo rejected.
Merge lineage intact and unrelated title retained.
Proposal alone does not move memories.
No memberships changed by dismissal.
Specified memory moves to separate branch.
Previous membership restored and branch history retained.
Archived-memory split rejected.
Stale split cannot override correction.
Second resolution rejected without duplicate event.
Optimistic sequence guard rejects stale decision.
All expected state and original event payloads survive restart.
Named singleton retained; no immediate repeated placement.
Cancellation appends no organization event; old policy refreshes once.

state_machine.note: A generated command can contain restore prerequisites. Fifty is the number of generated commands, not database writes. Merge/split/cancellation are covered in explicit cases, not randomized model operations.

limitations: Fixture merge and split proposals isolate correction integrity; they do not assess automatic proposal semantics.
Original filenames/revision references are checked; media file content restoration is not exercised because the current restoration API uses the personal app's default library path.
Recap generation is not invoked, avoiding live local language-model calls; generic citation integrity is asserted when citations exist.
Unavailable retries are immediate; this suite does not certify wall-clock backoff timing or the daily batch scheduler.
